title: SIMULIA 316-steel shouldered axisymmetric ratcheting specimen
purpose: Exercise the complete geometry-to-result Chaboche route against a public shouldered-specimen experiment while keeping plotted-data uncertainty and numerical convergence independent.
physics: axisymmetric small-strain 316-steel combined-hardening plasticity under asymmetric cyclic end pressure

source.title: Uniaxial ratcheting under tension and compression

MFront mechanical behaviours and implicit integration

Homogenization of two-phase elasto-plastic composite materials and structures: study of tangent operators, cyclic plasticity and numerical algorithms

execution.evidence: The self-contained mesh reconstructs the public dimensions; the optional official input deck is accepted only when its SHA-256 matches the recorded identity.

observables: Absolute and root-mean-square difference from digitized experimental Figure 4 points.
Independent spatial-mesh and accuracy-driven path-integration changes.
acceptance: The structure result remains inside the AgentFEM-defined absolute curve-error band after including raster uncertainty.
The final Newton residual is below the declared equilibrium tolerance.
The final two spatial meshes and maximum-plastic-increment limits each change the cycle-peak strain by no more than the declared release tolerance.
limitations: SIMULIA publishes Figure 4 as a raster plot rather than a numerical table; AgentFEM records a conservative digitization uncertainty.
The public Abaqus input uses CAX4R/CAX3 and geometric nonlinearity; AgentFEM uses an independently generated triangular meridian mesh and the current small-strain Chaboche formulation.

Fixed-step development runs exposed load-path sensitivity. The five-cycle adaptive gate now passes with all 17 physical knots reached, 0.290% change between the final two maximum-plastic-increment limits, 0.192% spatial-mesh change, and an equilibrium residual below 1e-9.

The 245-cell, 100-cycle response reaches all 302 mandatory physical coordinates with 533 accepted increments and 8 transactional cutbacks; its maximum PEEQ increment is 9.54e-4, final equilibrium residual is 9.23e-10, and maximum absolute difference from the digitized curve is 1.205e-3 against the predeclared 1.25e-3 gate.

The 100-cycle curve passes the AgentFEM-defined raster-data gate narrowly; absent a vendor numerical table and like-for-like element/kinematic formulation, this remains external comparison evidence rather than an exact Golden or automatic material-maturity promotion.
